name: Partnership-Agreement
content:
PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT

Background:

This Partnership Agreement (“Agreement”) is made as of this [INSERT DATE] between:

Partner(s) ____________ located at ____________ and

____________ located at ____________ and

____________ located at ____________ and

____________ located at ____________ and

____________ located at ____________ (each, a “Partner” and collectively, the “Partners”).

Partnership details

  1. The Partners agree to form a partnership under the name of [INSERT NAME]. The Partnership will be governed in accordance with the laws of the State of [INSERT STATE]. The Partnership is formed on the terms and conditions in the Agreement below, to engage the business of ____________ [INSERT BUSINESS] to engage in any and all necessary activities to carry on the business of the Partnership.

Place of business

  1. The principal office of the Partnership will be located at [INSERT ADDRESS], or at such places as the Partners shall determine from time to time.

Term

  1. The Partnership shall commence on [INSERT DATE] and continue until [INSERT DATE] OR [it is terminated in accordance with the terms of this agreement].

Partners’ Capital Contributions

  1. The Partners will contribute capital to the Partnership within [DAYS] of the Effective Date, on or before [DATE].
  2. The Partner’s cash contribution will be:
    1. [NAME OF PARTNER], [AMOUNT].
    2. [NAME OF PARTNER], [AMOUNT].
    3. [NAME OF PARTNER], [AMOUNT].
    4. [NAME OF PARTNER], [AMOUNT].
  3. The Partner’s non-cash contribution and the value:
    1. [NAME OF PARTNER], [DESCRIPTION], [AMOUNT].
    2. [NAME OF PARTNER], [DESCRIPTION], [AMOUNT].
    3. [NAME OF PARTNER], [DESCRIPTION], [AMOUNT].
    4. [NAME OF PARTNER], [DESCRIPTION], [AMOUNT].

Partner’s Capital Accounts

  1. The Partnership will establish and maintain for each Partner a separate capital account made up of the Partner’s capital contributions. A Partner may not withdraw any portion of capital at any time without written consent of all Partners.
  2. [No interest will be paid on the capital account of any Partner].

Profits and losses

  1. Net profits and losses will be divided [Equally between the Partners] OR [according to the same proportion as the Partner’s capital contributions to the Partnership].

Partner’s Income Accounts

  1. [Interest, at the rates and times as determined by the Partners will be paid on the income account of any Partner.] OR [No interest will be paid on the income account of any Partner.]

Partner’s Salary and Drawings

Salary

  1. [PARTNER NAME] will receive a salary of [INSERT AMOUNT] per [INSERT TIMESCALE].

[PARTNER NAME] will receive a salary of [INSERT AMOUNT] per [INSERT TIMESCALE].

[PARTNER NAME] will receive a salary of [INSERT AMOUNT] per [INSERT TIMESCALE].

[PARTNER NAME] will receive a salary of [INSERT AMOUNT] per [INSERT TIMESCALE].

Profits

  1. [A Partner may withdraw any portion of profits from their income account at any time] OR [A Partner may withdraw any portion of profits from their income account at any time but only with the prior written consent of all Partner’s] OR [The Partnership will distribute profits to Partners at the end of each [INSERT TIMESCALE]].

Partnership Bank Accounts

  1. The Partnership funds will be kept in an account in its name at [INSERT DETAILS] or at any other institution as agreed between the Partners.

Partnership Books and Records

  1. The Books and records of the Partnership will be kept and maintained at [INSERT LOCATION].
  2. Such books and records will be available for inspection by [any Partner or his or her representative] OR [any Partner during business hours with reasonable notice].
  3. The Partnership shall maintain its books and records in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
  4. The Partnership’s fiscal year will begin on [DATE] and close on [DATE]. An income statement and balance sheet will be prepared at the end of each fiscal year within [MONTHS] after the end of the fiscal year.

Management

  1. Each Partner has equal rights in the management of the Partnership. The Partners will devote as much time as is reasonable to the affairs of the Partnership to accomplish the objectives of the Partnership.
  2. Each Partner has the power to make [only significant] OR [only ordinary] OR [significant and ordinary decisions on behalf of the Partnership].
  3. All Partner’s agree to take the following Partnership actions:
    1. [Enter into, make, and perform any contract or agreement including lease, security agreement, or mortgage];
    2. [Borrow or lend money];
    3. [Sell all, or substantially all of the assets of the Partnership other than that sold in the regular course of the Partnership’s business];
    4. [Hiring and firing employees].

Voluntary Dissolution of Partnership

  1. The Partnership may be dissolved at any time upon the consent of [all Partner’s] OR [a majority of Partner’s] OR [INSERT OTHER]. The Partner’s shall, as soon as is reasonably Practical, liquidate and wind up the affairs of the Partnership. The proceeds received in connection with the liquidation and any other remaining assets of the Partnership will be applied in the following order of priority:
    1. Payment of all debts, liabilities, and obligations of the Partnership. This includes all expenses of liquidation;
    2. Distribution to or for the benefit of the Partners in accordance with the positive balance in each Partner’s income account;
    3. Distribution to the benefit of the Partners in accordance with the positive balance in each Partner’s capital account.

Partner’s withdrawal

  1. A Partner may withdraw from the Partnership [at any time] OR [after a period of [INSERT PERIOD] OR [INSERT OTHER] by providing at least [DAYS] written notice of such intention to the other Partner’s. The remaining Partner’s will have the decision to either dissolve and liquidate the Partnership with the withdrawing Partner or continue the Partnership by purchasing and withdrawing Partner’s interest. The decision requires the unanimous consent of the remaining Partner’s. If the remaining Partners whose to withdraw Partners Interest, the remaining Partners shall provide written notice of such intention to purchase within [DAYS] after receipt of the withdrawing Partner’s notice to withdraw.

OR

A Partner may not withdraw from the Partnership unless all Partners agree to the withdrawal. If the remaining Partner’s agree, the remaining Partner’s will have the decision to either dissolve and liquidate the Partnership with the withdrawing Partner or continue the Partnership by purchasing and withdrawing Partner’s interest. The decision requires the unanimous consent of the remaining Partner’s. If the remaining Partners whose to withdraw Partners Interest, the remaining Partners shall provide written notice of such intention to purchase within [DAYS] after receipt of the withdrawing Partner’s notice to withdraw.

OR

A Partner’s withdrawal from the Partnership will terminate the Partnership. The Partnership will be dissolved, and the assets liquidated.

Involuntary Withdrawal

  1. [Not applicable] OR [a Partner may be removed from the Partnership if such partner: [commits fraud], [Declares Bankruptcy], [Is declared incompetent], [Commits embezzlement], [is imprisoned]].
  2. The remaining Partners may decide either to dissolve and liquidate the Partnership with the removed Partner or continue the Partnership by purchasing the removed Partner’s interest. The decision to dissolve or continue the Partnership requires the unanimous consent of the remaining Partners. If they choose to purchase the removed Partner’s interest, the remaining Partners shall provide written notice of such intention to purchase within [DAYS] after knowledge of the Partner’s removal.

Partner’s Retirement

  1. A Partner may retire from the Partnership [at any time] OR [at the end of the Partnership’s fiscal year] OR [at the end of a calendar month] OR [only after a period of [YEARS] from the date of this Agreement] by providing at least [DAYS] written notice of such intention to the other Partner’s. The remaining Partner’s have the decision to either dissolve and liquidate the Partnership with the retiring Partner or continue the Partnership by purchasing the retiring Partners interest. The decision requires the unanimous consent of the remaining Partner’s. If the remaining Partners whose to purchase the retiring Partners Interest, the remaining Partners shall provide written notice of such intention to purchase within [DAYS] after receipt of the retiring Partner’s notice to retire.

Partner’s Death

  1. If the Partner dies, the remaining Partners have the decision to either dissolve and liquidate the Partnership, or continue the Partnership by purchasing the deceased Partners interest. The decision requires the unanimous consent of the remaining Partner’s. If the remaining Partners whose to purchase the deceased Partners Interest, the remaining Partners shall provide written notice of such intention to purchase within [DAYS] after the Partner’s death to the administrator or executor of the deceased Partner’s estate.

Buyout

  1. If the remaining Partner’s choose to purchase the withdrawing, retiring or deceased Partner’s interest, that interest will be purchased in [equal amounts by all remaining Partners] OR [the amounts as decided by all remaining Partners] OR [the amounts as decided by the remaining Partners that wish to purchase].

Buyout Price Assessment

  1. Restriction on Transfer

New Partners

Arbitration

Binding Effect

  1. This Agreement shall be binding upon the benefit of the Partner and their respective legal representatives, heirs, administrators, executors, successors and permitted assigns.

Severability

  1. If any provision of this Agreement becomes invalid, illegal or unenforceable in whole or in part, the remaining provisions shall not be affected and shall continue to be valid, legal and enforceable.

Governing Law

  1. The terms of this Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with the laws of the state of [INSERT STATE], not including its conflicts of law provisions.

Further Assurances

  1. At the written request of one Partner, the other Partners shall execute and deliver such necessary documents to affect the terms of this Agreement.

Headings

  1. The section headings are for reference purposes only and shall not otherwise affect any provision in this Agreement.

Entire Agreement

  1. This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the Partners, and supersedes all prior agreements of the Partners, whether they be oral or written agreements.

Counterparts

  1. This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed as the original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same document.

Amendment

  1. This Agreement may be amended or modified only by a written agreement signed by all of the Parties.

Notices

  1. Any notice or other communication given to a party in connection with this Agreement shall be in writing, and shall be:
    1. Delivered either by hand, by pre-paid first-class post, or by other next working day delivery service, at the receiving party’s postal address provided in this Agreement unless otherwise stated; or
    2. Sent by email to the email address specified in writing.

Waiver

  1. A waiver of any right or remedy under this Agreement or by law is only effective if given in writing and shall not be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach.
  2. A failure or delay by a party to exercise any right or remedy provided under this Agreement or by law shall not constitute a waiver of that or any other right or remedy.

PARTNERSHIP DISSOLUTION AGREEMENT

This Partnership Dissolution Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and effective this [DATE],

BETWEEN:

[SELLING PARTNER NAME] (the "Selling Partner"), a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the [STATE/PROVINCE], with its head office located at:

AND:

[PURCHASING PARTNER NAME] (the "Purchasing Partner"), a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the [STATE/PROVINCE], with its head office located at:

RECITALS

  1. The parties are partners in the firm of [NAME], of [ADDRESS], [CITY], [STATE], established for the purpose of [SPECIFY], under an agreement dated [DATE].

  1. Pursuant to the terms of the partnership agreement, a buy or sell notice was given by Selling Partner to Purchasing Partner.

  1. The Purchasing Partner has exercised its option to purchase the interest of Selling Partner in and to the partnership business.

In consideration of the matters described above, and of the mutual benefits and obligations set forth in this agreement, the parties agree as follows:

1. SALE OF INTEREST; PURCHASE PRICE

Selling Partner shall sell its [__%] interest in the partnership business, including its [__%] interest in all of the furniture, equipment, and furnishings of the business, stock of merchandise, accounts receivable, moneys, and all of ________ [SELLING PARTNER NAME’S] right, title, and interest in and to any and all of the assets of the partnership, to Purchasing Partner for ________ [AMOUNT], to be paid in ________ [NUMBER] equal monthly installments, due on the ________ [SPECIFY] day of each month, commencing on ________ [DATE].

2. ASSUMPTION OF OBLIGATIONS

The Purchasing Partner shall and do assume and agrees to pay all of the outstanding debts and obligations of the partnership business and to perform all of the covenants of the leases on the premises, and to perform all of the outstanding contracts and agreements required to be performed by the partnership and agrees to save and hold harmless Selling Partner against any claim or claims that may arise by reason of such debts, obligations, or covenants, or any other claims except those specifically mentioned in this agreement.

OF LAW.

3. INDEMNIFICATION

The Selling Partner warrants and represents that it has incurred no debts, nor contracted any obligations, nor incurred any liability in the name of the partnership or for which the partnership would be liable, other than those debts, obligations, or liabilities as are disclosed in the partnership books of which Selling Partner has advised the Purchasing Partner. The Selling Partner agrees to indemnify and save and hold harmless the Purchasing Partner on account of any claims that may be made against the partnership because of any debt, obligation, or liability which the Selling Partner incurred in the partnership name or for which the partnership became liable on account of any of ________ [SELLING PARTNER NAME’S] actions and of which Selling Partner failed to inform the Purchasing Partner.

4. TAX RETURNS AND PAYMENTS

The Purchasing Partner agrees to prepare federal and state partnership income tax returns for the partnership business from ________[DATE] to ________ [DATE], and to supply Selling Partner with copies. Each of the parties shall pay their individual income taxes, both federal and state, on the income received from such partnership business.

5. ASSUMPTION OF TAX OBLIGATIONS

The general taxes and all other tax obligations shall be considered an obligation of the partnership and are now assumed by the Purchasing Partner.

6. DISSOLUTION

The partnership existing between the parties under the name of ________ [PARTNERSHIP NAME] is dissolved and this agreement constitutes a full and complete accounting and liquidation of the partnership business. Except as otherwise reserved in this agreement, Selling Partner acknowledges that it has no claim or demand of any kind or nature against Purchasing Partner. Also except as otherwise reserved in this agreement, Purchasing Partner acknowledges that it has no claim or demand of any kind against Selling Partner.

7. GOVERNING LAW

This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of [STATE/PROVINCE OF GOVERNING LAW].

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have executed this Partnership Dissolution Agreement as of the date first above written.

SELLING PARTNER PURCHASING PARTNER

PARTNERSHIP DISSOLUTION AGREEMENT

This Partnership Dissolution Agreement (the “Dissolution Agreement”) is made on ____________, 20__ (the “Dissolution Date”) by and between by and between _________________________, a _______________________________________[corporation] [limited liability company] [etc.] ( “Partner One”), and _______________________, a ______________________________ [corporation] [limited liability company] [etc.] (the “Partner Two”) (each a “Partner” and collectively the “Partners” ).

RECITALS

WHEREAS, the Partners entered into that certain partnership agreement dated as of (the “Partnership Agreement”), relating to the Partnership (as defined below) for the purpose of ________________________________________________________________________________; and

WHEREAS, under the terms of the Partnership Agreement, Partner One made capital contributions totaling ____________;

WHEREAS, under the terms of the Partnership Agreement, Partner Two made capital contributions totaling ____________;

WHEREAS, pursuant to the terms of the Partnership Agreement, the Partners have __________________________________________; and

WHEREAS, the Partners now wish to dissolve and terminate the Partnership (as defined below) pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Partnership Agreement and this Dissolution Agreement;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the mutual agreements and representations contained herein, the Partners hereby agree as follows:

    1. DISSOLUTION.

In accordance with this Dissolution Agreement and the terms of the Partnership Agreement, the Partners hereby agree that effective as of the Dissolution Date, that certain partnership, which was formed under the laws of ____________________, did business under the name of __________________________, and had its principal business address at ______________________________________________________________________ (the “Partnership”), shall dissolve in accordance with Section[s] ________________ of the Partnership Agreement.

    1. WINDING UP.

Effective as of the Dissolution Date, all (a) assets, rights, and properties owned by the Partnership on the Dissolution Date whether tangible or intangible, real, personal, or mixed, wherever located, and whether or not carried and reflected on the books of the Partnership, including, without limitation, all accounts receivable, inventory, equipment and improvements, contract rights, claims, and causes of action or rights of recovery or set-off of every kind and character, and all business records (collectively, the “Partnership Assets”) shall be distributed to the Partners pro rata in accordance with their respective ownership interests in the Partnership; and (b) all obligations and liabilities of the Partnership, whether known or unknown, whether asserted or unasserted, whether absolute or contingent, whether accrued or unaccrued, whether liquidated or unliquidated and whether due or to become due (collectively, the “Partnership Liabilities” and each a “Partnership Liability”) shall be distributed to the Partners pro rata in accordance with their respective ownership interests in the Partnership.

    1. LIQUIDATING PARTNER[S].

[Partner One] [Partner Two] [The Partners together] (the “Liquidating Partner[s]”) shall coordinate and be [solely] responsible for the liquidation of the Partnership Assets, the satisfaction of the Partnership Liabilities, and such other acts as may be reasonably required to wind up the affairs of the Partnership. Prior to the Dissolution Date, the following business matters will be completed by the Liquidating Partner[s]:______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________. In addition, the Liquidating Partner[s] will record and publish a notification of Dissolution of Partnership in a local newspaper and submit a Statement of Dissolution to the Secretary of State.

    1. (Optional) CUSTODIAN OF PARTNERSHIP BOOKS.

[Partner One] [Partner Two] shall be named the official custodian of the records of the Partnership for at least ________ years following the Dissolution Date.

    1. INDEMNIFICATION.

Each Partner hereby indemnifies and holds harmless the other Partner from and against any claims, demands, actions, losses, or damages suffered by such other Partner as a result of the Partner’s failure to pay and discharge any part of a Partnership Liability that such Partner has assumed under this Dissolution Agreement.

    1. RELEASE AND DISCHARGE.

The Parties hereby release and forever discharge one another from any and all claims, demands, actions, losses, or damages arising from or relating to the Partnership; provided, however, that each Partner remains responsible for any claims, demands, actions, losses, or damages arising or resulting from the terms and conditions of this Dissolution Agreement.

    1. AMENDMENTS.

This Dissolution Agreement may be amended only with the unanimous written consent of the Partners.

    1. GOVERNING LAW.

This Dissolution Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state of _____________, without regard to its conflicts of law provisions.

    1. NO IMPLIED WAIVER.

The failure of any Partner to insist on strict performance of any covenant or obligation under this Dissolution Agreement, regardless of the length of time for which such failure continues, shall not be a waiver of such Partner’s right to demand strict compliance in the future. No consent or waiver, express or implied, to or of any breach or default in the performance of any obligation shall constitute a consent or waiver to or of any other breach or default in the performance of the same or any other obligation.

    1. COUNTERPARTS/ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES.

This Dissolution Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument. For purposes of this Dissolution Agreement, use of a facsimile, e-mail, or other electronic medium shall have the same force and effect as an original signature.

    1. SEVERABILITY.

In the event that any provision of this Dissolution Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable for any reason, (i) the invalid or unenforceable provision or term shall be replaced by a term or provision that is valid and enforceable and that comes closest to expressing the intention of such invalid or unenforceable term or provision and (ii) the remaining terms and provisions hereof shall be unimpaired and shall remain in full force and effect.

    1. HEADINGS.

The headings of sections in this Dissolution Agreement are provided for convenience of reference only and are not intended to be a part of or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Dissolution Agreement or any section.

    1. ENTIRE AGREEMENT.

This Dissolution Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between the Partners concerning its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions, agreements, and representations, whether oral or written and whether or not executed by any Partner. No modification, amendment, or other change may be made to this Dissolution Agreement unless reduced to writing and executed by authorized representatives of all Partners.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Partners have executed this Dissolution Agreement as of the date first above written.

4. Parties Bound

This Agreement shall be binding on, and inure to the benefit of, the Partners and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns.

 

5. Strict Construction

ARTICLE IV. TERM OF AGREEMENT; DEFAULT; TERMINATION

4.1 Term. Unless sooner terminated in accordance with its provisions, the Term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue in effect until expiration of the term of the last Patent to expire of the patents listed in Schedule A of this Agreement.

4.2 Default; Cure. If a party is in default of any obligations under this Agreement, the non-defaulting party may give written notice of such default to that party. After notice is provided, the party in default shall have thirty (30) days to cure any defaults arising from any failure to make any royalty payment pursuant to this Agreement, and sixty (60) days to cure any other defaults. If such default is not cured within the applicable thirty (30) days or sixty (60) days after the date of such notice, then the non-defaulting party shall have the option to terminate this Agreement after providing notice of such termination to the party in default.

4.3 Bankruptcy; Insolvency. This Agreement may be terminated by a party if the other party is at any time placed into bankruptcy, goes into voluntary dissolution, has a receiver appointed, or makes any general assignment for the benefit of creditors.

In the event this Agreement terminates because Licensor no longer has a Patent Right on which royalties are due, then Licensee is under no obligation to pay royalties or cease using, importing, making, having made, offering for sale, and selling Products.

4.5 Releases; Survival of Certain Obligations. ARTICLE VI. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY

6.1 Assumption of Risk. As between the parties, Licensee assumes full responsibility for all risk and liability in relation to the Products and all loss of or damage to property or injury to persons related to the Products including, but not limited to, death arising out of Licensee’s manufacture and sale of Products. Licensee shall indemnify, defend and hold Licensor harmless from and against any and all claims, costs (including court costs, expert fees, and attorneys’ fees), proceedings and liabilities, whatsoever, for and arising out of any such loss, damage, injury, or death related to the Products.

description: This Public–Private Partnership Contract (the “Contract”) is executed on _______________ [Insert Date], by and between [--- Government Entity ---], hereinafter referred to as the “Government,” and [--...
content:
Public–Private Partnership Contract

This Public–Private Partnership Contract (the “Contract”) is executed on _______________ [Insert Date], by and between [--- Government Entity ---], hereinafter referred to as the “Government,” and [--- Private Representative Name ---], representing [--- Private Company Name ---], hereinafter referred to as the “Private Partner.”

1. Purpose

The purpose of this Contract is to define the terms and conditions governing collaboration between the Government and the Private Partner for the development, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of a major infrastructure project (the “Project”).

2. Background

2.1 Project Description

The Project involves the design and implementation of a large-scale transportation infrastructure system spanning a considerable distance, including the construction of transit routes, facilities, supporting technology, and procurement of equipment. It is intended to enhance regional connectivity and promote economic development.

2.2 Rationale for Partnership

The Government seeks to leverage private sector expertise, innovation, and financial resources to deliver and manage the Project effectively, while safeguarding public interests.

3. Scope of Work

3.1 Development Phase

The Private Partner shall be responsible for:

  • Conducting studies and assessments
  • Securing permits and approvals
  • Preparing detailed project documentation
  • Identifying and mitigating risks
  • Creating implementation schedules
  • Procuring materials and services
  • Coordinating with stakeholders
  • Reporting progress
  • Delivering agreed outcomes

3.2 Construction Phase

The Private Partner shall construct the Project in accordance with approved designs and specifications.

3.3 Operation and Maintenance Phase

Following construction, the Private Partner shall operate and maintain the Project for the duration specified in this Contract.

4. Financing Arrangements

4.1 Investment Obligations

The Private Partner shall finance the development and implementation of the Project, including all related costs.

4.2 Government Contributions

The Government may provide contributions, incentives, or other forms of support in accordance with separate agreements or as outlined in this Contract.

4.3 Revenue Sharing

Revenue generated from the Project shall be distributed between the parties based on terms agreed within this Contract or supplemental documentation.

5. Performance Standards

5.1 Quality Compliance

The Project must meet or exceed applicable quality standards and comply with relevant technical and regulatory requirements.

5.2 Service Levels

The Private Partner shall ensure that services related to the Project are consistently reliable and efficient throughout the Term.

5.3 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Metrics shall be established to evaluate the Private Partner’s performance, including service availability, reliability, safety, and user satisfaction.

6. Risk Allocation

6.1 Force Majeure

The Contract shall include provisions to address unforeseen events beyond the reasonable control of the parties. These provisions shall outline relief mechanisms and responsibilities.

6.2 Insurance Requirements

The Private Partner shall maintain adequate insurance coverage, including but not limited to construction risk, liability, and performance-related policies.

6.3 Dispute Resolution

Dispute resolution procedures shall be specified, including potential use of mediation, arbitration, or alternative resolution mechanisms.

7. Term and Termination

7.1 Term of Contract

The Contract shall commence on [Insert Start Date] and shall remain in effect until [Insert End Date], unless earlier terminated according to the terms herein or by mutual consent.

7.2 Termination Events

Either party may terminate this Contract in the event of material breach, insolvency, or force majeure, subject to any required notice provisions and dispute resolution efforts.

8. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

This Contract shall be governed by the laws of [--- Jurisdiction ---]. All disputes shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the competent courts in [--- Location ---].

9. Miscellaneous Provisions

9.1 Confidentiality

Each party agrees to maintain confidentiality regarding any proprietary or sensitive information shared during the course of this partnership.

9.2 Assignment

Neither party may assign or delegate its rights or obligations without prior written consent of the other party.

9.3 Amendment

This Contract may be amended only by a written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Contract through their duly authorized representatives as of the date first written above.

content:
Public–Private Partnership Agreement

This Public–Private Partnership Agreement (“Agreement”) is made effective as of ____________ (the “Effective Date of Contract”), by and between:

[--- Name of Public Entity ---] (hereinafter referred to as the "Public Owner"), and
[--- Name of Private Entity ---] (hereinafter referred to as the "Private Entity").

Project Overview

The Public–Private Project that is the subject of this Agreement generally involves the management and oversight of a public utilities department, including planning, design, construction management, financial assistance, operational support, maintenance oversight, and the administration of day-to-day activities associated with such infrastructure (the “Project”).

Facilities Included in the Project

As part of the Project, oversight and management responsibility shall be transferred to the Private Entity for the following existing facilities and infrastructure:

  • Wastewater Treatment Plant A
  • Wastewater Treatment Plant B
  • Water Treatment Facility
  • Water Distribution System Infrastructure, including potable water lines, valves, hydrants, elevated water storage tanks, pump stations, and related components
  • Sewer Collection and Conveyance System Infrastructure, including gravity lines, manholes, lift stations, force mains, and other assets
  • Sewer Pre-Treatment Systems

ARTICLE 1 – DEFINITIONS

1.01 Standard Definitions

Wherever used in this Agreement, capitalized terms have the following meanings:

  1. Agreement – This written instrument executed by the Public Owner and Private Entity, describing the Project and establishing mutual obligations.
  2. Concession – The rights and obligations granted to the Private Entity by the Public Owner under this Agreement.
  3. Concession Term – The duration during which the Concession remains valid (see Article 3).
  4. Constituent of Concern – Any hazardous material, substance, or waste that is regulated under applicable environmental laws and regulations.
  5. Constructor – Any party involved in or supporting construction activities, including contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, and service providers.
  6. Contract – The comprehensive and integrated written agreement between the parties concerning the Project.
  7. Contract Documents – All documents explicitly referenced or incorporated into the Agreement as part of the contractual framework.
  8. Design and Construction Management – All services required for the design and construction oversight of Project facilities, including necessary testing, documentation, and commissioning.
  9. Laws and Regulations – All applicable legal requirements, including statutes, regulations, codes, permits, and administrative orders.
  10. Project – The scope of tasks and responsibilities undertaken by the Private Entity as described herein.
  11. Relief Event – Any occurrence during the Concession Term that justifies an adjustment to the Concession or other contractual provisions.
  12. Site – The physical areas designated for use in the Project, including existing facilities, rights-of-way, and other locations designated for Private Entity’s use.

ARTICLE 2 – PROJECT REQUIREMENTS

2.01 Project Requirements

The Public Owner hereby contracts with the Private Entity for the operation and management of the Public Owner’s utility infrastructure, which includes:

  • Wastewater treatment facilities
  • Water treatment facilities
  • Distribution and conveyance systems
  • Associated systems and equipment for water and wastewater services

2.02 Public Owner’s Policies and Procedures

The Public Owner shall provide applicable internal policies and procedures relevant to the Private Entity’s scope of work, and the Private Entity shall comply with such requirements.

ARTICLE 3 – PUBLIC OWNER’S GRANT OF CONCESSION; CONCESSION TERM

3.01 Grant of Concession

Subject to the terms of this Agreement, the Public Owner grants to the Private Entity the exclusive right and responsibility to:

  1. Provide qualified personnel for the ongoing operation and maintenance of the public utility infrastructure;
  2. Oversee emergency projects as needed;
  3. Direct certain Public Owner personnel in day-to-day activities;
  4. Manage the Public Utility Department in coordination with designated representatives of the Public Owner.

The Private Entity shall provide the following minimum personnel:

  • One Utilities Department Division Manager (licensed professional engineer registered per jurisdictional requirements)
  • One Water Treatment Division Manager (with appropriate operator license)
  • One Wastewater Treatment Division Manager (also responsible for Pre-Treatment)
  • One Lift Station Division Manager
  • One Distribution and Collection System Division Manager
  • Additional personnel as necessary to meet performance obligations under this Agreement.

3.02 Concession Term

A. The Concession Term shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for five (5) years, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions herein.

B. During the Concession Term, the Private Entity shall provide an annual report to the governing authority summarizing the status of the Public–Private Partnership and overall performance of the utility systems under its management.

C. Upon completion of the initial term, the Agreement may be renewed by mutual consent of the parties, subject to renegotiated terms and conditions.

ARTICLE 4 – PUBLIC OWNER’S RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

4.01 General

A. The Public Owner shall be responsible for, and the Private Entity may rely upon, the accuracy and completeness of all requirements, programs, instructions, reports, data, and other information furnished by the Public Owner under this Agreement. The Private Entity may use such information in performing its obligations.

B. The Public Owner shall give prompt written notice to the Private Entity upon becoming aware of:

  1. Any event or development affecting the scope or timing of the Private Entity’s responsibilities;
  2. Any defect or nonconformance in the Private Entity’s performance;
  3. The presence at any Project site of any Constituent of Concern.

C. The Public Owner shall retain ownership of all Project sites and shall not lease any such sites to the Private Entity. The Public Owner shall provide the Private Entity with access and operational control over the sites for the duration of the Concession Term.

D. The Public Owner shall support necessary site acquisition activities, including the exercise of eminent domain rights if applicable. The Private Entity shall assist by procuring boundary surveys or similar property-related services at the Public Owner’s expense.

E. The Public Owner shall make all decisions and fulfill responsibilities in a timely manner to avoid delay to the Private Entity’s performance.

4.02 Review and Oversight

A. Submittals (including but not limited to change orders, directives, pay applications, reports, and correspondence) prepared by the Private Entity shall comply with agreed requirements. The Public Owner shall review submittals promptly and respond in writing by:

  1. Approving;
  2. Conditionally approving (with specific reasons); or
  3. Rejecting, based on inconsistencies with Project Requirements or material terms.
    Approval shall not modify the Project Requirements unless expressly stated.

B. The Public Owner shall not be liable for identifying technical deficiencies in the Private Entity’s work. The Private Entity shall correct such deficiencies without additional compensation unless they arise from inaccurate Public Owner-furnished information.

ARTICLE 5 – OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE

5.01 Staffing

A. The Private Entity shall ensure the Project Facilities are adequately staffed with certified and qualified personnel. A staffing plan (organizational chart) indicating both Private Entity and Public Owner personnel shall be submitted and approved. (See Exhibit C.)

B. Staff shall be available as necessary to comply with applicable regulations.

5.02 Training and Safety

A. The Private Entity shall provide ongoing training to designated Public Owner personnel related to operations, safety, and compliance.

5.03 System and Equipment Operation

A. The Private Entity shall operate systems in accordance with manufacturer and designer recommendations.

B. Maintenance activities shall preserve warranty rights, including proper documentation and adherence to recommended schedules.

5.04 Inspections and Monitoring

A. The Private Entity shall perform routine inspections of the Project Facilities.

B. Bi-annual performance and condition reports shall be submitted to the Public Owner.

5.05 Maintenance

A. Preventive and corrective maintenance shall be managed and overseen by the Private Entity.

B. Detailed maintenance records for all facilities and equipment shall be maintained.

C. The Private Entity shall submit regulatory maintenance reports as required.

5.06 Cleaning and Waste Removal

A. The Project Facilities shall be kept clean and orderly by the Private Entity.

B. Waste disposal shall comply with applicable regulations. The Public Owner shall cover the cost of necessary waste removal from public facilities.

5.07 Records and Reporting

A. All required records and reports shall be maintained and submitted by the Private Entity in accordance with applicable laws and the Agreement.

ARTICLE 6 – FACILITIES MANAGEMENT

6.01 General Duties

A. The Private Entity shall perform all general administrative, accounting, staffing, and budgeting functions related to the Project unless otherwise provided.

6.02 Project Additions

A. The Private Entity shall plan, design, and manage the bidding and construction of new or upgraded infrastructure projects.

B. The Public Owner shall review and approve new project plans and funding allocations per internal governance procedures.

ARTICLE 7 – REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

7.01 Private Entity Representations

The Private Entity represents that:

A. It has reviewed all Contract Documents and referenced data.

B. It has examined Project Sites and is familiar with site conditions.

C. It understands and is prepared to comply with all relevant laws and regulations.

D. The Contract Documents adequately define the Project requirements.

E. It has conducted financial and technical due diligence, possesses the necessary resources and licenses, or can subcontract appropriately.

ARTICLE 8 – ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITION OF SITE

8.01 Encountering a Constituent of Concern

A. The Public Owner has disclosed all known or suspected Constituents of Concern, including location and quantity.

B. The Public Owner affirms that, to its knowledge, no other such constituents exist on-site.

C. Upon encountering an undisclosed constituent, the Private Entity shall notify both the Public Owner and any applicable authorities, if required.

D. The Public Owner shall address any undisclosed constituents it knew of or suspected but failed to disclose, including costs of mitigation.

E. For constituents discovered post-Effective Date with no prior knowledge by either party, both parties shall collaborate to determine the appropriate response. Cost-sharing shall be determined based on factors such as responsibility for site selection and investigation.

ARTICLE 9 – INSURANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION

9.01 General Insurance Provisions

A. All insurance policies shall include provisions preventing cancellation or modification without prior written notice (minimum 10 days). Copies of such notices shall be promptly shared by the receiving party.

B. Upon written request and at the Public Owner’s expense, the Private Entity shall procure additional or enhanced insurance coverage as commercially available. Exhibit A shall be amended accordingly.

9.02 Private Entity Insurance

A. The Private Entity shall maintain the insurance specified in Exhibit A and provide proof of coverage before commencement of work and upon renewals.

B. The Public Owner shall be named as an additional insured on applicable general liability policies.

C. The Private Entity shall require its contractors and consultants to carry adequate insurance and name both the Public Owner and Private Entity as additional insureds.

9.03 Indemnification

A. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Private Entity shall indemnify and hold harmless the Public Owner and its representatives from all third-party claims, including legal fees, arising from acts or omissions of the Private Entity or its affiliates, including but not limited to:

  1. Breach of this or related contracts
  2. Violation of laws or regulations
  3. Infringement of intellectual property
  4. Negligence, misconduct, or fraud
  5. Release of environmental contaminants
  6. Interference with third-party operations

B. Indemnification shall not apply to:

  1. Acts of negligence or misconduct by the indemnified party
  2. Regulatory violations by the indemnified party
  3. Material breach of the contract by the Public Owner

C. The Private Entity is not liable for regulatory fines or orders unless directly caused by its own negligence.

ARTICLE 10 – ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFER; NO THIRD-PARTY BENEFICIARIES

10.01 Successors, Assigns, and Beneficiaries

A. The Public Entity and the Private Entity and their respective successors, executors, administrators, legal representatives, and assigns shall be bound to one another in respect of all obligations under this Contract.

10.02 Transfer by Public Entity

A. To the extent permitted by applicable law, the Public Entity may, upon no less than –– days’ advance written notice to the Private Entity, assign, transfer, or delegate its rights and obligations under this Contract to another entity, provided such entity is capable of performing the obligations herein without impairing the interests of the Private Entity.

10.03 Transfer by Private Entity

A. The Private Entity shall not assign, transfer, pledge, encumber, or otherwise convey any interest in this Contract, in whole or in part, voluntarily or involuntarily, without the prior written consent of the Public Entity, except:

  1. As required by applicable law;
  2. As security to lenders consistent with this Contract, provided the Private Entity remains liable for performance;
  3. To an affiliated entity under common management or control.

B. Unless specifically waived in writing, no such assignment shall release the assigning party from its duties under the Contract.

C. All permitted transfers are subject to the Public Entity's review to ensure consistency with Contract goals and the public interest.

10.04 No Third-Party Beneficiaries

A. Unless expressly stated:

  1. This Contract does not confer any benefit or enforceable rights upon any third party.
  2. Obligations herein exist solely between the Public Entity and the Private Entity.

ARTICLE 11 – CHANGES

11.01 Relief Events

A. Either party may seek modifications to the Contract (including the Concession Term) based on a Relief Event, by submitting a proposed amendment describing the basis and rationale for such change.

11.02 Administration of Proposed Contract Changes

A. Upon identifying a potential Relief Event, the initiating party shall notify the other in writing without delay.

B. A formal Change Proposal shall follow, outlining proposed adjustments and supporting documentation.

C. The parties shall meet to discuss and negotiate the proposal in good faith.

D. If unresolved, the proposing party shall submit a final written proposal. The receiving party shall approve or reject it within 30 days. Failure to respond will be considered a rejection.

E. If rejected, the proposing party may initiate dispute resolution procedures under Article 12.

ARTICLE 12 – FINAL RESOLUTION OF DISPUTES

12.01 Unresolved Change Proposals

A. If a Change Proposal is denied and the procedures in Paragraph 12.02 are followed, the dispute may proceed under this Article.

12.02 Mediation

A. All disputes shall first be submitted to mediation using a mutually agreed mediator. The parties shall mediate in good faith, confidentially, and within –– days of initiating mediation. Mediation costs shall be shared equally.

12.03 Final Resolution

A. If mediation fails:

  1. The parties may agree on an alternative resolution method; or
  2. Either party may seek judicial resolution in a court of competent jurisdiction.

ARTICLE 13 – MISCELLANEOUS

13.01 Governing Law

A. This Contract shall be governed by the laws of the [Insert Governing Jurisdiction], without regard to conflicts of law provisions.

13.02 Compliance with Laws

A. Both parties shall comply with all applicable laws, codes, ordinances, and regulations.

13.03 Notices

A. All notices must be in writing and delivered personally, by certified mail, or by a reputable courier to the address specified in the signature section. Notice is effective upon receipt.

13.04 Survival

A. All indemnities, waivers, limitations of liability, and express representations shall survive termination or completion of this Contract.

13.05 Severability

A. If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall remain enforceable. The invalid term shall be replaced with a valid term reflecting the parties’ intent.

13.06 Waiver

A. Failure to enforce any provision does not waive the right to enforce it later.

13.07 Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages

A. Each party waives all claims for consequential, incidental, or special damages against the other, including lost profits or indirect losses.

13.08 Direct Damages Permitted

A. Claims related to unpaid compensation or mitigation of lost services shall be considered direct damages and are recoverable.

13.09 Independent Contractor

A. The Private Entity is an independent contractor and not a partner, agent, or employee of the Public Entity.

13.10 Use of Contractors and Consultants

A. The Private Entity may retain contractors or consultants necessary for performance, subject to reasonable objection by the Public Entity.

13.11 Electronic Transmittals

A. Electronic communications may be used to exchange project-related materials via email or secure platforms under mutually agreed protocols.
B. No guarantee is made regarding the compatibility of digital files with systems used by the receiving party.

13.12 Designated Representatives

A. Each party shall designate an authorized representative to manage Contract communications and make decisions on behalf of their respective organizations.

ARTICLE 14 – SUSPENSION AND TERMINATION

14.01 Suspension

A. The Public Entity may suspend the Project for up to –– days by giving at least –– days’ written notice.

B. The Public Entity shall reimburse the Private Entity for demobilization, remobilization, and other equitable costs incurred as a result of the suspension.

14.02 Termination

A. Termination for Cause:

  1. Either party may terminate with 30 days written notice for substantial breach by the other party.
  2. The defaulting party may cure the breach within a 30–60 day period if such cure is diligently pursued.
  3. Upon termination for cause, the Private Entity shall assign all control over Project Facilities to the Public Entity, including documentation transfer.

B. Termination for Convenience:

The Public Entity may terminate at its sole discretion with written notice.

C. Termination Effective Date:

The terminating party may set the termination date up to 30 days after the notice to allow for demobilization and documentation transfer.

D. Payment Upon Termination:

  1. The Private Entity is entitled to payment for services performed and reimbursable costs incurred through the effective date of termination, including the present value of any improvements paid for by the Private Entity.
  2. If terminated for convenience or by the Private Entity for cause, the Private Entity is also entitled to reasonable termination-related costs.

ARTICLE 15 – CONTRACT DOCUMENTS

15.01 Composition of Contract

A. The Contract includes this executed Agreement and its incorporated Exhibits.

15.02 Included Exhibits

A. Exhibit A – Insurance Requirements
B. Exhibit B – Payment Terms and Reimbursable Expenses
C. Exhibit C – Organizational Chart

15.03 Entire Agreement

A. This document represents the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both parties.

name: materials purchasing agent agreement
content:
MATERIALS PURCHASING AGENT AGREEMENT

This Materials Purchasing Agent Agreement (“Agreement”) is made as of __________, 20, by and between [OWNER NAME], a _____________ entity (“Owner”), and [CONTRACTOR NAME], a _____________ corporation (“Agent”).

RECITALS

A. The Owner and the Agent have entered into a separate agreement for construction services dated __________, 20 (the “Construction Agreement”), for the construction of the project known as [PROJECT NAME], identified as Project No. _____________ (the “Project”).

B. The Project is to be constructed in accordance with the drawings and specifications prepared by [ARCHITECT OR DESIGN PROFESSIONAL NAME] (the “Design Professional”), and as supplemented by additional documents incorporated into the Construction Agreement (collectively, the “Contract Documents”).

C. The Owner intends to purchase certain materials, supplies, and equipment to be used in the Project in order to obtain direct purchase tax advantages or for other reasons.

D. The Owner desires to appoint the Agent to act as its purchasing agent solely for the acquisition of those materials, supplies, and equipment described in this Agreement, and the Agent is willing to do so on the terms set forth herein.

AGREEMENT

1. Incorporation of Terms


All terms defined in the Contract Documents shall apply to this Agreement unless otherwise modified. The provisions of this Agreement shall control in the event of any conflict with the Contract Documents regarding the subject matter herein.

2. Appointment of Purchasing Agent


The Owner appoints the Agent as its purchasing agent solely for the acquisition of those materials, equipment, and supplies listed in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated by reference (the “Materials”).

3. Duties of the Agent


The Agent shall:

  • Procure the Materials on behalf of the Owner in accordance with the Contract Documents and construction schedule.
  • Solicit competitive quotes or bids for Materials where applicable.
  • Consult with the Owner prior to issuing any purchase orders.
  • Coordinate deliveries and storage of Materials at the Project site or other designated locations.

4. Compensation


The Owner agrees to pay the Agent an amount equal to:
a.The actual cost of the Materials;
b.A fee of % of the cost of the Materials (“Agent’s Fee”); and
c.Reimbursement for the Agent’s personnel and administrative costs directly associated with the purchasing services, at the hourly rates listed in Exhibit B, not to exceed a total amount of ______.

5. Title and Risk of Loss


Title to all Materials purchased under this Agreement shall vest in the Owner at the point of delivery. Risk of loss for the Materials shall remain with the Owner following delivery, except in cases of negligence or willful misconduct by the Agent.

6. Warranties and Acceptance


The Agent makes no warranty as to the Materials but shall exercise reasonable care in their inspection upon receipt. Final acceptance of the Materials remains with the Owner or its representative. The Agent shall assist in resolving any warranty claims or defects, as directed by the Owner.

7. Storage and Protection


The Agent shall exercise reasonable care in the safekeeping of Materials under its control prior to incorporation into the Project. The Agent shall be responsible for loss or damage due to its failure to take such care.

8. Sales and Use Tax Exemption


If applicable, the Owner and Agent shall coordinate to ensure that purchases made under this Agreement qualify for any applicable tax exemptions. The Agent shall complete any required exemption certificates and include appropriate language on all purchase orders to reflect that purchases are being made on behalf of a tax-exempt owner. Sample language may be provided by the Owner.

9. Invoicing and Payment


The Agent shall:

  • Collect invoices from vendors and submit payment applications to the Owner;
  • Disburse payments to suppliers upon receipt of funds from the Owner;
  • Maintain proper documentation and provide a summary of Materials purchased, including any tax savings obtained.

10. Accounting and Records


The Agent shall maintain accurate records of all purchases and payments made under this Agreement, and shall make such records available to the Owner upon request. Funds provided by the Owner shall be held in trust and used solely for payment of the Materials.

11. Defective or Nonconforming Materials


The Owner shall be responsible for defective or nonconforming Materials unless caused by the Agent’s negligence or failure to follow specifications. The Agent shall notify the Owner promptly of any such issues and assist in remedying them.

12. Indemnification


The Owner shall be responsible for any sales or use tax assessed on the Materials unless due to the Agent’s failure to follow applicable procedures or instructions. The Owner shall indemnify and hold harmless the Agent from such taxes or penalties, except as otherwise provided.

13. Dispute Resolution


Any disputes arising under this Agreement shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution provisions set forth in the Construction Agreement.

14. Termination


This Agreement may be terminated by either party upon written notice, subject to the completion of any outstanding purchasing obligations and payments for approved and performed services.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

procurement of the following: (the "Products"). The Purchasing Agent shall procure the said Products on behalf of the Company in accordance with the instructions given by the Company. Purchasing Agent does hereby accept such appointment and agrees to act as Purchasing Agent under the terms and conditions specified in this Agreement.

TERM

This Agreement shall be in effect as of the date set forth above, and shall continue for a period of --- years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall be automatically renewed on a yearly basis thereafter. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time upon giving ____ (0) days notice, in writing to the other party.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Purchasing Agent shall:

  1. Negotiate with independent manufacturers, suppliers and vendors with respect to prices, terms and deliveries for the Products;
  2. Enter into purchasing contracts with independent manufacturers and vendors with respect to Products;
  3. Inspect the Products destined for shipment and delivery to Company for quality control purposes and issue inspection certificates certifying that the Products conform to purchase contracts or order;
  4. When requested, arrange for international transportation and/or appropriate insurance coverage, relating to shipment and delivery of the Products to Company;
  5. Perform any and all other services and activities (including negotiations relating thereto and payment therefor) agreed to in writing by and between Company and Purchasing Agent.

INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR

Purchasing Agent shall provide the Services as an independent contractor and Purchasing Agent shall not act as an employee, Purchasing Agent or broker of the Company. As an independent contractor, Purchasing Agent will be solely responsible for paying any and all taxes levied by applicable laws on its compensation. Purchasing Agent understands that Company will not withhold any amounts for payment of any taxes from Purchasing Agent's compensation.

PAYMENT

During the term of this Agreement, Company shall pay the Purchasing Agent for its Services under this Agreement the sum of ------. Payment shall be made by the --- day of the month following receipt of Purchasing Agent's invoice for the Services.

EXPENSES

The Company agrees to reimburse any pre-approved out of pocket expenses incurred by the Purchasing Agent in connection with the Services, including, but not limited to, travel expenses, audit fees, tax fees, payroll service fees, etc.

CONFIDENTIALITY

Purchasing Agent in the course of performing the Services hereunder may gain access to certain confidential or proprietary information of the Company. Such "Confidential Information" shall include all information concerning the business, affairs, products, marketing, systems, technology, customers, end-users, financial affairs, accounting, statistical data belonging to the Company and any data, documents, discussion, or other information developed by Purchasing Agent hereunder and any other proprietary and trade secret information of Company whether in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machinereadable form. The Purchasing Agent agrees to hold all such Confidential Information of the Company in strict confidence and shall not, without the express prior written permission of Company,

  1. disclose such Confidential Information to third parties; or
  2. use such Confidential Information for any purposes whatsoever, other than the performance of its obligations hereunder. The obligations under this Section shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement.

TERMINATION

  1. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by providing ____ (0) days written notice ("Termination Notice") to the other party.
  2. If a party violates its obligations to be performed under this Agreement, the other party may terminate the Agreement by sending a ___ (0) days notice in writing. Upon receiving such notice, the defaulting party shall have ___ (0) days from the date of such notice to cure any such default. If the default is not cured within the required thirty (30) day period, the party providing notice shall have the right to terminate this Agreement.

ASSIGNMENT

Purchasing Agent shall not assign any of their rights under this Agreement, or delegate the performance of any of the obligations or duties hereunder, without the prior written consent of the Company and any attempt by Purchasing Agent to so assign, transfer, or subcontract any rights, duties, or obligations arising hereunder shall be void and of no effect.

NOTICES

Any notices, bills, invoices, or reports required by this Agreement shall be deemed received on (a) the day of delivery if delivered by hand during receiving party's regular business hours or by facsimile before or during receiving party's regular business hours; or (b) on the second business day following deposit in the United States mail, postage prepaid, to the addresses heretofore below, or to such other addresses as the parties may, from time to time, designate in writing pursuant to the provisions of this section.

Company:

Purchasing Agent:

GOVERNING LAW

This Agreement is to be construed in accordance with and governed by the internal laws of the State of -

DISPUTE RESOLUTION

All disputes under this Agreement shall be settled by arbitration in ------ before a single arbitrator pursuant to the commercial law rules of the __________ Arbitration Association. Arbitration may be commenced at any time by any party hereto giving written notice to the other party to a dispute that such dispute has been referred to arbitration. Any award rendered by the arbitrator shall be conclusive and binding upon the parties hereto. This provision for arbitration shall be specifically enforceable by the parties and the decision of the arbitrator in accordance herewith shall be final and binding without right of appeal.

SEVERABILITY

If any provision of this Agreement shall be held to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable under present or future laws, such provisions shall be fully severable, this Agreement shall be construed and enforced as if such illegal, invalid or unenforceable provision had never comprised a part of this Agreement; and, the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect.

LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, LOSS OF OR UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS TO INFORMATION, DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, INCURRED BY THE OTHER PARTY ARISING OUT OF THE SERVICES PROVIDED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. IN NO EVENT WILL NEITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ON ANY CLAIM, LOSS OR LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR CONNECTED WITH THIS AGREEMENT SHALL EXCEED THE AMOUNTS PAID TO PURCHASING AGENT.

INDEMNIFICATION

Each party shall at its own expense indemnify and hold harmless, and at the other party's request defend such party its affiliates, subsidiaries, successors and assigns officers, directors, employees, sublicensees, and Purchasing Agents from and against any and all claims, losses, liabilities, damages, demand, settlements, loss, expenses and costs (including attorneys' fees and court costs) which arise directly or indirectly out of or relate to (a) any breach of this Agreement, or (b) the gross negligence or willful misconduct of a party's employees or Purchasing Agents;

ENTIRE AGREEMENT; AMENDMENT

This Agreement is the final, complete and exclusive agreement of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes and merges all prior or contemporaneous representations, discussions, proposals, negotiations, conditions, communications and agreements, whether written or oral, between the parties relating to the subject matter hereof and all past courses of dealing or industry custom. No modification of or amendment to this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by each of the parties.

WAIVER

The waiver by either party of a breach of or a default under any provision of this Agreement shall not be effective unless in writing and shall not be construed as a waiver of any subsequent breach of or default under the same or any other provision of this Agreement, nor shall any delay or omission on the part of either party to exercise or avail itself of any right or remedy that it has or may have hereunder operate as a waiver of any right or remedy.

CAPTIONS

The headings used in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not be used to limit or construe the contents of any of the sections of this Agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have signed this Agreement as of the date first set forth above.

name: Automotive Quality Assurance Agreement
content:
Quality Assurance Agreement
between
--- [Customer/Buyer] ---
and
--- [Supplier] ---

Concerning the implementation of a joint quality management system to ensure consistent product development and product quality.

Preamble

This Quality Assurance Agreement (QAA) defines the technical and organizational framework between the parties required to meet the intended quality objectives. It sets out minimum requirements for the management systems of both parties, with emphasis on product and production process quality assurance.

General Agreements

Scope of Applicability, Object of Agreement

  • This agreement applies to all locations of the Customer.
  • It defines quality requirements for all development services and/or products delivered during the contractual period.
  • In case of discrepancies, individually negotiated agreements take precedence. Any modifications or additions must be made in writing.
  • This QAA supplements any applicable development and supply agreements or purchasing terms.
  • The Supplier acknowledges and agrees to follow applicable guidelines provided by the Customer for the cooperation and handling of purchased parts.

Supplier's Quality Management System

  • The Supplier commits to a zero-defect goal and continuous improvement.
  • A functional Quality Management (QM) system must be in place.
  • Valid third-party certifications must be submitted to the Customer and kept up to date.
  • The Supplier is also expected to adhere to generally accepted automotive industry requirements, such as __________ or equivalent.
  • Environmental standards such as __________ must be observed.
  • Any Customer-provided production and testing resources are to be integrated into the Supplier’s QM system.

Contact Persons and Project Organization

  • The Supplier shall appoint and communicate at least one project manager and one quality representative, along with designated substitutes.
  • Regular meetings between both parties shall occur during the project to review quality topics and develop procedural improvements. These meetings typically take place at the Supplier’s site and are scheduled by the Customer.

Quality Management System of Sub-suppliers

  • The Supplier must ensure sub-suppliers comply with equivalent quality requirements.
  • The Customer may request documentation demonstrating the effectiveness of sub-suppliers’ QM systems.

Audit Rights

  • The Customer has the right to conduct system, process, or product audits at the Supplier’s site with appropriate notice.
  • Audits by recognized certification bodies will be considered.
  • In case of sub-supplier-related quality issues, the Supplier agrees to audit the relevant sub-supplier.

Documentation and Information Obligations

  • Documentation and evidence relevant to quality must be retained for a period of at least __ years.
  • The Supplier must promptly inform the Customer of any risks to meeting contractual obligations or quality standards.
  • The Supplier must report any increase in quality deviations or planned changes in production processes, materials, or suppliers.
  • All product or process changes affecting quality must be recorded in a product history log, in accordance with industry standards.

Product Development and Planning

  • For development tasks, requirements must be formally defined.
  • The Supplier will implement project management procedures and allow access to planning schedules upon request.
  • Technical documentation must be reviewed for completeness and clarity; any issues must be communicated to the Customer.
  • Preventive quality planning tools should be used such as, feasibility studies, and capability analysis.
  • Production conditions for prototype and pre-production parts must be agreed upon.
  • Process and product capability analyses must be conducted for critical features.
  • Pre-series approval processes must follow applicable industry practices (e.g., PPAP or equivalent).

Series Production and Traceability

  • In the event of process disruptions or quality deviations, root cause analysis and corrective measures must be implemented and verified.
  • Traceability systems must be in place and effective based on risk assessment.
  • Packaging and labeling must follow agreed identification requirements.
  • Requalification testing must be conducted annually unless otherwise agreed.

Audits, Complaints, and Quality Programs

  • An audit plan should be jointly agreed upon to support quality objectives.
  • The Supplier must use methods (e.g., SPC or equivalent) to demonstrate process capability for critical features.
  • If capability cannot be maintained, 100% inspection is required, along with corrective process improvements.
  • All products must be free from material, structural, or processing defects and meet all contractual specifications.
  • Defective parts may be returned for analysis; disputes are to be jointly resolved.
  • A Quality Improvement Program (QIP) may be initiated by the Customer in the event of significant quality performance issues. This includes setting ppm targets and corrective actions to restore compliance.

Duration of Agreement

This agreement is valid for an indefinite period and may be terminated by either party with three months' written notice. Termination does not affect the validity of active individual supply agreements until their obligations are fully met.

name: Electronics Quality Assurance Agreement
content:
ELECTRONICS QUALITY ASSURANCE AGREEMENT

Between __________________ located at __________________ (hereinafter referred to as the Supplier) and _______________ [customer/s] located at _______________ (hereinafter referred to as the Customer).

Preface

The competitiveness and position of our customers in the world market is decisively influenced by the quality of its products. The faultless quality and reliability of purchased components have a direct influence on the overall quality of its end-use applications.

This Quality Assurance Agreement is a statement of the fundamental technical and organizational conditions detailing ___________ [Supplier]Electronics’ deliveries and services to our customers that are geared towards an intended quality objective of “zero defects”. It describes policies and procedures currently in place as a basis for ____________Supplier’s total quality management system.

The conclusion of this Quality Assurance Agreement represents an indispensible step for a continued successful business relationship with our customers.

Contents

1. Supplier’s responsibility for the quality of delivered products 4

2. Scope of the agreement 4

3. Supplier’s Quality Management System 4

3.1 Procurement Policies 4

3.2 Vendor Evaluations 5

4. Packaging, Labeling and Transport 5

5. Zero Defect Strategy 5

6. Customer Complaint / Returned Product Analysis Process 6

7. General Provisions 6

Supplier’s responsibility for the quality of delivered products

The supplier is responsible for providing products and services which are free from defects, in accordance with component OEM technical documents. All products must comply with original manufacturer specifications in form, fit and function.

The quality strategy of the supplier must be oriented towards continuous improvement of its processes and services. The objectives are “zero defects”, 100% delivery performance and the reduction of costs.

The supplier also undertakes to meet promised deadlines, e.g. for delivery of samples, shipping of customer orders, introduction of corrective measures, documentation requests.

Scope of the agreement

This agreement is entered into by the Customer’s Purchasing department and ___________ [Supplier]Electronics, LLC. and applies to all components and products delivered to the customer by the supplier.

Supplier’s Quality Management System

Procurement Policies

The supplier currently purchases components for inventory or to fulfill customer orders from the following sources:

  • Manufacturer direct
  • Franchised distributors
  • OEM/EMS excess
  • Approved independent distributors
  • ___________________________...

Direct manufacturer and franchised distribution channels generally have low risk and require minimum quality assurance protocols. OEM/EMS excess stock must have full traceability to component manufacturers or franchised distributors. Supplier overlooks delivery and storage of documentation to prove the origin of components procured from OEM/EMS excess stock. Approved independent distributors must undergo an extensive appraisal including the following factors:

  • Industry position
  • Better Business Bureau (professional ethics)
  • ERAI Status
  • Financial Stability
  • Dunn & Bradstreet Rating
  • Bank & Trade references
  • _____________________________...

Approved independent distributors must also provide full traceability documentation and/or full test reports on a case-by-case basis.

Vendor Evaluations

Independent distributors are stored in supplier’s vendor database utilizing an A through F grading system.

Approved vendors are evaluated quarterly for quality, performance, and delivery. Supplier uses a statistical process control in correlation to alphabetic grade to upgrade or downgrade approved vendors.

Supplier agrees to procure only from A or B rated vendors. B rated vendors must go through corrective action planning in an effort to achieve A rated status.

Packaging, Labeling and Transport

The supplier will ensure that the quality of the products is not impaired in the course of transportation to the relevant customer point of receiving or through just-in-time delivery or vendor-managed-inventory delivery to ongoing production.

The supplier shall deliver solely in packaging compliant with manufacture specifications and ensure safe handling as to minimize any damage incurred during transport. Further, the supplier will use only the mode of transport and shipping details as agreed upon with the customer.

All electro-static sensitive devices shall be properly packaged to provide protection from electrostatic discharge. Material packaging shall not negatively influence material quality or include any impurities. Moisture sensitive devices shall be packaged in an ESD Moisture Barrier Bag and labeled appropriately.

Zero Defect Strategy

The supplier undertakes that its TQM system, policies, and procedures commits to the “zero defect” strategy.

Supplier shall use statistical process controls and supporting process capability analysis to achieve continuous quality improvement and failure rate reductions. Customer may define the method used in reporting quality goals and the means expressing the results such as DPPM or percentages.

Supplier shall maintain and make available upon request outgoing quality inspection, reliability records, and applicable data as defined within this document and provide such data to customer upon request.

Customer Complaint / Returned Product Analysis Process

Supplier shall investigate and drive resolution to any customer complaints or returned product occurrences in a timely manner. Supplier agrees to provide a corrective and preventative action plan that responds to complaints received from customer.

Supplier shall apply appropriate problem-solving techniques to identify root causes and implement permanent corrections.

General Provisions

Any modifications or side agreements shall require written form. In the event that any provision of this Quality Assurance Agreement is invalid or may become invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions shall not be affected thereby and shall remain valid.

The parties commit themselves, in good faith, to replace any invalid provision with a valid provision that has an economic result equivalent to the original provision.
